answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a small refundable deposit before it can take paid work, released only after verified peers attest the work was real. That deposit is the bridge between a cheap new identity and a costly one: a single honest kernel of reputation, built from completed jobs and peer attestations, accumulates over time and cannot be cloned for free. A flood of fake identities is like an ocean of empty shells; without deposits and history they stay locked out of paid work, while honest agents keep their stake and keep earning.
